items.title: Nepal Red Cross to build 1,000 temporary shelters and 1,000 permanent homes for flood victims
items.summary: Kathmandu, October 15 The Nepal Red Cross Society will build 1,000 temporary shelters and 1,000 permanent homes for families affected by floods in Rasuwa and the Bhotekoshi area. According to Bishal Kumar Bhandari, chairperson of the society’s central ad hoc committee, an agreement was signed with the Department of Building under the Ministry of Physical […] The post Nepal Red Cross to build 1,000

items.title: How will Nepal verify those missing after the Bhotekoshi floods?
items.summary: The government has begun compiling an official list of people missing in the August 26 disaster. The process will determine who can be declared dead and whose families qualify for relief.

items.title: Contractor builds 268-metre suspension bridge in a month after floods cut off communities
items.summary: Shailendra Raj Pyakurel tapped the construction industry’s own fund to build a vital crossing over the Trishuli river for Rs17.5 million, nearly half the government’s estimate.

items.title: Father cannot afford last rites for son missing in Bhotekoshi floods
items.summary: Forty-seven days after 25-year-old Pradip Sapkota went missing, his family has yet to recover his body and is struggling to pay for his funeral rites.

items.title: Makawanpur begins process to declare 58 missing people dead
items.summary: Authorities have begun verifying the status of those missing since the August 26 Bhotekoshi floods under a special government procedure, with local units required to collect applications and check claims.

items.title: Relief helicopter gives Rasuwa farmers a route to market
items.summary: The WFP has flown around eight tonnes of vegetables from flood-isolated Aamachhodingmo to Bidur, helping growers salvage part of their harvest.

items.title: Salyan villages have little heart for Dashain celebrations
items.summary: Dozens remain missing after the Bhotekoshi floods in Rasuwa, leaving families and neighbours across the district with little to celebrate this year.
